message.content:
The idea of a “best” movie is inherently subjective—different people value different things (story, acting, technical craft, cultural impact, etc.).  Below is a quick snapshot of some of the most critically acclaimed and widely celebrated films released in 2020, along with a few key metrics that many people use when judging a movie’s quality.  (All figures are approximate and reflect the state of the data as of mid‑2024.)

| Film | Director | Rotten Tomatoes (Critics) | Metacritic | Notable Awards / Nominations |
|------|----------|---------------------------|------------|------------------------------|
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | 94 % | 78 | 3 Oscars (Best Original Screenplay, Best Supporting Actor, Best Supporting Actress) |
| **The Father** | Florian Zeller | 95 % | 84 | 2 Oscars (Best Actor – Anthony Hopkins, Best Supporting Actress – Olivia Colman) |
| **Nomadland** | Chloé Wang | 93 % | 81 | 3 Oscars (Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actress – Frances McDormand) |
| **Soul** | Pete Docter, Kemp Garnett | 98 % | 88 | 1 Oscar (Best Animated Feature) |
| **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | 70 % | 66 | 1 Oscar (Best Visual Effects) |
| **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | 86 % | 71 | 1 BAFTA (Best Production Design) |
| **Mulan** (Disney live‑action) | Niki Adjei‑Brennan | 73 % | 61 | 1 BAFTA (Best Production Design) |
| **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | 84 % | 73 | 1 Oscar (Best Supporting Actor – Mads Mikkelsen) |

### How to decide “best”

| Criterion | What it measures | Example |
|-----------|------------------|---------|
| **Critical consensus** | Aggregated reviews from professional critics | Rotten Tomatoes score |
| **Audience reception** | General viewer ratings | IMDb rating, CinemaScore |
| **Awards** | Recognition by industry bodies | Oscars, BAFTAs, Golden Globes |
| **Cultural impact** | Influence on society, memes, discussions | Social media buzz, box‑office performance |
| **Personal preference** | Genre, storytelling style, emotional resonance | Your own taste |

If you’re looking for a film that performed exceptionally well across most of these dimensions, **“The Father”** and **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** are often cited as the standout releases of 2020.  Both earned multiple Academy Awards and received high marks from critics and audiences alike.

If you prefer animation, **“Soul”** topped the charts with a 98 % Rotten Tomatoes score and an Oscar for Best Animated Feature.  For a more action‑heavy, mind‑bending experience, **“Tenet”** was a polarizing but technically impressive entry.

Ultimately, the “best” movie for you will depend on what you value most in a film.  Feel free to let me know if you’d like recommendations tailored to a specific genre or mood!
